tours.title: Private Tour: Cliffs of Moher & Galway
tours.lede: Twelve and a half hours across Ireland, in a vehicle that carries nobody but your group. You leave before the coaches and reach the cliffs while the light is still low.
tours.metaDesc: A private 12.5-hour day from your Dublin hotel to the Cliffs of Moher, the Burren and Galway city. One vehicle, up to 16 people, from €790. Price by group size.
tours.ogDesc: Leave Dublin at 7am, stand on the Cliffs of Moher before the coaches arrive, and walk Galway in the afternoon. Private, up to 16 people.
tours.ribbonLabel: Dublin 07:00 — Dublin 19:30
tours.stopsIntro: A guide, not a timetable. Your driver will stretch a stop you love and skip one you don't.

stops.p: We collect you from your hotel. The early start is the whole trick: it puts you on the west coast before the tour coaches get there.
A fifteenth-century tower house, complete and intact, on the road west.
Two hundred metres of sheer Atlantic rock, running eight kilometres along the coast. You have long enough to walk out to O'Brien's Tower and back without hurrying.
A limestone pavement that looks like nowhere else in Ireland, with a portal tomb standing in the middle of it since before the pyramids.
A small harbour village with a castle sitting on the water's edge. The photograph everyone takes on this road.
Two hours on foot through the old town with your guide, then time of your own. Seafood, street musicians on Shop Street, and the pubs that earned Galway its reputation for traditional music.
Dropped where you were collected. Roughly — traffic on the M6 decides the last half hour.

tours.includedIntro: The price covers the vehicle.
included: Private vehicle and driver-guide for the whole day
Pick-up and drop-off at your Dublin hotel
Entrance to the Cliffs of Moher
Guided walking tour of Galway city
Itinerary changed on the day, as you like
tours.notIncluded: Lunch and drinks are not included — there's a stop in Doolin or Galway for that, and your guide will tell you where's good.
practical: Any hotel or address in Dublin city. Tell us where when you book.
Most of the day suits most travellers. The cliff path is uneven in places — tell us about any mobility needs and we'll plan around them.
The tour runs in rain. Bring a coat and shoes you don't mind getting wet.
faq: Does the price depend on the size of the group?
Yes. The tour is private, and the price depends on how many of you travel, starting from €790. Choose the number of people when you book.
Can we change the stops?
That's the point of a private tour. Tell your guide in the morning, or decide at lunch. The only fixed parts are the Cliffs of Moher timing and getting you home.
What if it rains?

It will, at some point. The tour runs anyway — the cliffs in moving weather are better than the cliffs in flat sunshine. We only cancel for conditions that make the roads unsafe, and then you're refunded in full.
Are there more than 16 of us?
We run it in two vehicles travelling together, on one booking. Message us with the numbers and we'll send a price.

tours.title: Private Tour: Belfast, Titanic & Giant's Causeway
tours.lede: North across the border for the day: forty thousand basalt columns on the Antrim coast, the ship that was built here, and the city that built it.
tours.metaDesc: A private 13-hour day from Dublin to the Giant's Causeway, Titanic Belfast and the city itself. Both entrances included, up to 16 people, from €840.
tours.ogDesc: The Giant's Causeway, the Titanic museum and Belfast, in one private day from Dublin. Up to 16 people.
tours.ribbonLabel: Dublin 07:00 — Dublin 20:00
tours.stopsIntro: A guide, not a timetable. Tell your driver what matters most and the day moves around it.

stops.p: An early start, because the Causeway is three hours north and worth having to yourself for a while.
Forty thousand interlocking basalt columns where a volcano cooled sixty million years ago. The legend says a giant built it. Entrance is included.
One of the great drives in Europe, with Dunluce Castle on its cliff and the glens opening up on the inland side.
Built on the slipway where the ship itself was built. Nine galleries, from the shipyard to the wreck on the seabed. Your ticket is included.
Two hours through a city that has changed more than almost any in Europe. The murals, the Cathedral Quarter, and the pubs that have been there through all of it.
Roughly. It's a long day and the border traffic decides the last stretch.

Thirteen hours, with about six of them driving. Worth knowing if you're travelling with small children.

tours.title: Wicklow & Glendalough Private Day Tour
tours.lede: An hour from the city and the country changes completely: a monastic valley, a waterfall, and a mountain road that film crews keep coming back to.
tours.metaDesc: A private 7-hour day from Dublin through the Wicklow Mountains to Glendalough, Powerscourt and Lough Tay. Up to 16 people, from €630. Price by group size.
tours.ogDesc: Glendalough, Powerscourt Waterfall and the Sally Gap, in a private day from Dublin. Up to 16 people.
tours.ribbonLabel: Dublin 07:00 — Dublin 14:00
tours.stopsIntro: The shortest of our Irish days, and the one with the least driving between stops.

stops.p: None of this is far, so the day has room for an extra stop if you want one.
Formal gardens laid out in the eighteenth century, and the highest waterfall in Ireland at the other end of the estate.
A mountain pass across open bog, with nothing built on it. The road people picture when they picture Wicklow.
The dark lake with the white sand beach at one end, which is why it's called the Guinness Lake. The Vikings in the television series were filmed here.
A sixth-century monastic city in a glacial valley, with its round tower still standing. Time to walk to the upper lake and back.
Or dropped anywhere in Dublin you'd rather be.

Glendalough is as much walking as you want it to be — ten minutes or two hours. The paths to the upper lake are flat and good.
Travellers with one day and no appetite for six hours in a car. Everything here is within an hour of Dublin.

Can we add somewhere else?
Seven hours leaves room. Avoca, Kilruddery or the coast road through Greystones all fit. Ask your guide.
Is it good in winter?

Are there more than 16 of us?
Two vehicles travelling together, on one booking. Message us and we'll price it.

The forecourt and the Victoria Memorial. If the Changing of the Guard is on, your guide will time the morning around it.
Where every English coronation since 1066 has happened, with Big Ben and the Houses of Parliament across the road.
Nine hundred years of fortress, palace and prison on the Thames, with Tower Bridge beside it.
A pub or a cafe your guide actually rates, not the one with the queue outside. Your own time and your own bill.
The Rosetta Stone, the Parthenon sculptures and the Great Court. Free to enter, and the extra hours are what make it possible.
Street performers under the market roof, then the park on the way back if the weather holds.

tours.title: Private Tour: Sintra & Cascais
tours.lede: A hill of palaces built by kings who wanted somewhere cooler than Lisbon, the westernmost point of mainland Europe, and the coast road back along the Atlantic.
tours.metaDesc: A private 9-hour day from Lisbon to Sintra, Cabo da Roca and Cascais. Pena Palace, Quinta da Regaleira and the Atlantic coast. Up to 16 people, from €620.

stops.p: Out of the city before the Sintra road fills. It is only forty minutes, and arriving early is the whole difference.
A nineteenth-century royal palace painted red and yellow on top of a wooded hill, built by a king with Romantic tastes and no restraint. The views reach to the Atlantic.
A private estate full of symbols, with an inverted tower you walk down nine storeys into the ground. The strangest place in Portugal and the one people remember.
The old centre, the royal palace with its two chimneys, and a pastry shop that has been making travesseiros since 1862.
The westernmost point of mainland Europe: a cliff, a lighthouse, and a stone that says where the land ends and the sea begins.
A fishing town that became a royal resort, then a refuge for exiled kings. Back to Lisbon along the Atlantic, with the ocean on your right the whole way.
Or anywhere in Lisbon you would rather be dropped.

A working estate: how the grapes are still trodden by foot in some of them, how the wine is fortified, and why the port went downriver in flat-bottomed boats.
At a quinta or in a village, with the valley below. Your guide books it in the morning once you have said what you like.

A different scale from the first — usually a smaller, family-run estate, where the person pouring made the wine.
Roughly. Nobody has ever complained that this day ran long.

tours.metaDesc: A private six-hour tour of Madrid with your own driver-guide. The Royal Palace, the Prado quarter, Retiro and the Habsburg centre. From €590.

stops.p: The largest functioning royal palace in Europe by floor area, with the cathedral facing it across the square. Both exteriors are the point; going inside is optional.
The arcaded square that was the city's stage for four hundred years, and the lanes around it where the old taverns still are.
The Paseo del Prado with its three great museums on one boulevard, plus the Neptune and Cibeles fountains that Madrid's football clubs celebrate at.
The old royal gardens, with a glass pavilion built for an exhibition of plants from the Philippines and never taken down.

stops.h: Back where you want to be
stops.p: Your hotel, Gran Via, or wherever you are eating.

tours.title: Barcelona: Gaudí & Gothic Quarter Private Tour
tours.seoTitle: Barcelona Gaudi and Gothic Quarter Tour
tours.lede: Two Barcelonas in seven hours: the medieval one you walk, and the one a single architect invented and the city is still finishing.
tours.metaDesc: A private seven-hour tour of Barcelona with your own driver-guide. The Sagrada Familia, Park Guell, Casa Batlló and the Gothic Quarter. From €650.
tours.ogDesc: The Sagrada Familia, Park Guell and the Gothic Quarter, in seven private hours with your own driver-guide.
tours.ribbonLabel: Measured from your pick-up — you choose the hour
tours.stopsIntro: Gaudí's buildings are spread across the city and the Gothic Quarter is only walkable. That is exactly the shape a car and a guide solve.

stops.p: Collected from the door. Barcelona hotels and apartments anywhere in the city are fine.
A basilica begun in 1882 and still unfinished, which Gaudí knew he would never see completed. The Nativity facade is his; the Passion facade is not, and the difference is the argument.
A failed housing development that became the best park in the city: the mosaic bench, the hypostyle hall, and the view back over everything.
Casa Batlló and La Pedrera on the same boulevard, a hundred metres apart, by the same man. Nowhere else is modernisme this concentrated.
On foot with your guide: the cathedral, the Roman wall still built into the houses, and the squares you would walk past without being told what they are.

stops.h: Back where you want to be
stops.p: Your hotel, the Barceloneta, or wherever you are eating.

tours.title: Seville Private Day Tour
tours.lede: Eight hours in a city that was Moorish for five centuries and then spent the gold of the Americas on proving it was not. Both halves are still standing.
tours.metaDesc: A private eight-hour tour of Seville with your own driver-guide. The Alcázar, the cathedral and Giralda, Santa Cruz and the Plaza de España. From €600.

stops.p: Collected from the door, at the hour you pick.
The largest Gothic cathedral in the world, built on the footprint of the mosque it replaced — and the minaret they kept, and put a bell tower on top of.
A royal palace Christian kings built in Moorish style, still used by the Spanish royal family, and the oldest in Europe still in use. The gardens are half the visit.
The old Jewish quarter: whitewashed lanes barely wide enough for two, orange trees, and the courtyards you glimpse through iron gates.

stops.h: Plaza de España and María Luisa
stops.p: A half-circle of brick and tile built for the 1929 exposition, with a tiled alcove for every province in Spain. The park beside it is the city's shade.

stops.h: Back where you want to be
stops.p: Your hotel, Triana for the evening, or wherever you are eating.

tours.title: Rome Private Day Tour by Car
tours.seoTitle: Rome Private Day Tour by Car
tours.lede: Twenty-seven centuries in one city, and most of it a short walk from somewhere a car can stop. We drive the gaps, so the day is spent at the sites and not between them.
tours.metaDesc: A private eight-hour day in Rome with your own car and driver: the Colosseum and the Forum, the Pantheon, Trevi and St Peter’s, at your pace. From €420.

stops.h: The Colosseum and the Roman Forum
stops.p: The amphitheatre first, then the Forum and the Palatine Hill above it — the centre of the Roman world, still laid out street by street.
A temple nearly nineteen centuries old whose concrete dome is still the largest unreinforced one in the world. Five minutes away, a Roman stadium turned into a square with three Baroque fountains.

stops.h: Trevi, the Spanish Steps, and lunch
stops.p: The fountain is never empty and never less than worth it. Then the 135 steps up to Trinità dei Monti, and lunch in the streets below.
Bernini’s colonnade, and the basilica if the queue allows. Entry is free; shoulders and knees covered to go inside.

stops.h: Back where you want to be
stops.p: Your hotel, or dropped for dinner — Trastevere is ten minutes away.

tours.seoTitle: Pompeii and Amalfi Coast from Rome
tours.lede: The longest day we run in Italy, and the one people talk about afterwards: a Roman town stopped in a single afternoon in 79 AD, then a road cut into the cliffs above the sea.
tours.metaDesc: A private day trip from Rome to Pompeii and the Amalfi Coast with your own car and driver: the ruins in the morning, Positano after lunch. From €730.

Two hours in the excavated city — the forum, houses still painted inside, bakeries with their ovens, and Vesuvius over everything.
Across the Sorrento peninsula to the coast, and lunch above the sea.
The coast road, carved along the cliffs. The driver takes the bends; you take the window.
Houses stacked down the cliff to a single beach. Time to walk down, have a coffee, and be collected again at the top.
At your hotel in the evening.

tours.seoTitle: Tivoli: Villa d’Este and Hadrian’s Villa
tours.lede: Forty minutes east of Rome, two villas fourteen centuries apart: an emperor’s private city of pools and colonnades, and a cardinal’s garden where the water runs downhill through hundreds of fountains.
tours.metaDesc: A private six-hour trip from Rome to Tivoli with your own car and driver: Hadrian’s Villa and the fountains of Villa d’Este. From €870. Price by group size.

Built by the emperor Hadrian in the second century: baths, libraries, a theatre, and the Canopus, a long pool lined with statues. It covers more ground than Pompeii.
The old town on its hill, with a view back across the plain to Rome.
A Renaissance garden built for Cardinal Ippolito d’Este, terraced down the hillside — the Avenue of the Hundred Fountains, the Organ Fountain, and water everywhere you look.
At your hotel by mid-afternoon.

faq: Does the price depend on the size of the group?
Yes. The tour is private, and the price depends on how many of you travel, starting from €300. Choose the number of people when you book.
Can we do whale watching?
Yes, boats leave from Ponta Delgada in the morning. We can start the tour after you are back.
Can we split the island over two days?
Yes, and it makes for a gentler trip: the west one day, Furnas and the east the next.
Are there more than 16 of us?
Two vehicles travelling together, on one booking. Message us and we will price it.
